inspect.signature() function vs __code__ attribute Python

💡 Result:

Short comparison:

- inspect.signature(func)
  - Returns a high-level inspect.Signature with Parameter objects and return annotation; handles defaults, annotations, positional-only, VAR_POSITIONAL/KEYWORD, bound methods, functools.partial, and follows __wrapped__ by default. Raises ValueError if it can't produce a signature (some builtins/C-callables lack metadata). Also uses a func.__signature__ override if present. [1]

- func.__code__ (a code object)
  - Low-level immutable CodeType for Python-defined functions only. Exposes bytecode and raw internals (co_argcount, co_kwonlyargcount, co_varnames, co_flags, co_consts, co_firstlineno, etc.). Useful for bytecode/varname inspection but does not provide high-level Parameter/annotation semantics, and does not exist for built-in/C functions. [2]

When to use which:
- Use inspect.signature for portable, high-level callable introspection (argument names, kinds, defaults, annotations, binding).

+---
+schema_type: common
+title: "DVC Workflow Guide"
+tags:
+  - datasets
+  - infrastructure
+status: published
+owner: docs-team
+purpose: DVC workflow guide for dataset versioning and management.
+---
+
+**Data Version Control (DVC)** is used to track large datasets and model files without storing them in Git.
+
+## Setup
+
+DVC is initialized in this project with a local remote storage for development.
+
+```bash
+# DVC is already initialized
+# Remote storage configured at: .dvc/cache_local
+```
+
+## Tracked Datasets
+
+The following datasets are tracked with DVC:
+
+### Training Data
+- **Location**: `data/training/iqa_phase2/`
+- **DVC File**: `data/training/iqa_phase2.dvc`
+- **Size**: ~18.6 GB
+- **Files**: 50,003 files
+- **Purpose**: Phase 2 IQA training dataset with weak supervision labels
+
+### Benchmarks
+
+#### OHR-Bench
+
+- **Location**: `data/benchmarks/ohr-bench/`
+- **DVC File**: `data/benchmarks/ohr-bench.dvc`
+- **Size**: ~1.8 GB
+- **Purpose**: RAG-specific OCR benchmark for IQA evaluation
+
+#### OmniDocBench (Phase 3)
+
+- **Location**: `data/benchmarks/omnidocbench/`
+- **DVC File**: `data/benchmarks/omnidocbench.dvc`
+- **Size**: ~1.2 GB
+- **Purpose**: Comprehensive document understanding evaluation
+
+#### TableBank (Phase 2)
+
+- **Location**: `data/benchmarks/tablebank/`
+- **DVC File**: `data/benchmarks/tablebank.dvc`
+- **Size**: ~400 MB to 27 GB (depends on version)
+- **Purpose**: Table detection benchmark
+
+#### PubTabNet (Phase 2)
+
+- **Location**: `data/benchmarks/pubtabnet/`
+- **DVC File**: `data/benchmarks/pubtabnet.dvc`
+- **Size**: ~500 MB to 16 GB (depends on version)
+- **Purpose**: Table structure recognition benchmark
+
+#### FinTabNet (Phase 2)
+
+- **Location**: `data/benchmarks/fintabnet/`
+- **DVC File**: `data/benchmarks/fintabnet.dvc`
+- **Size**: ~3 GB to 11 GB (depends on version)
+- **Purpose**: Financial table detection and structure
+
+#### WiLI-2018 (Phase 2)
+
+- **Location**: `data/benchmarks/wili_2018/`
+- **DVC File**: `data/benchmarks/wili_2018.dvc`
+- **Size**: ~800 MB
+- **Purpose**: Language identification (235 languages)
+
+#### ICDAR MLT 2019 (Phase 2)
+
+- **Location**: `data/benchmarks/icdar_mlt_2019/`
+- **DVC File**: `data/benchmarks/icdar_mlt_2019.dvc`
+- **Size**: ~3 GB
+- **Purpose**: Multi-lingual text detection
+
+**Note**: Synthetic IQA datasets (auto-generated) and DocLayNet (symlinked) are NOT tracked in DVC.
+
+## Common Commands
+
+### Pull Datasets
+```bash
+# Pull all tracked datasets
+poetry run dvc pull
+
+# Pull specific dataset
+poetry run dvc pull data/training/iqa_phase2.dvc
+poetry run dvc pull data/benchmarks/ohr-bench.dvc
+```
+
+### Add New Data to Tracking
+```bash
+# Add a new dataset directory
+poetry run dvc add data/training/new_dataset
+
+# Commit the .dvc file to git
+git add data/training/new_dataset.dvc
+git commit -m "Add new dataset to DVC tracking"
+
+# Push data to remote storage
+poetry run dvc push
+```
+
+### Update Existing Data
+```bash
+# After modifying a tracked dataset
+poetry run dvc add data/training/iqa_phase2
+
+# Commit updated .dvc file
+git add data/training/iqa_phase2.dvc
+git commit -m "Update IQA training dataset"
+
+# Push updated data
+poetry run dvc push
+```
+
+### Check Status
+```bash
+# See which datasets have changed
+poetry run dvc status
+
+# See data cache status
+poetry run dvc cache dir
+```
+
+### Remove Data Locally (Keep Tracking)
+```bash
+# Remove local copy of dataset (keeps .dvc file)
+rm -rf data/training/iqa_phase2
+
+# Restore from DVC cache
+poetry run dvc pull data/training/iqa_phase2.dvc
+```
+
+## Remote Storage
+
+### Current Configuration
+- **Type**: Local filesystem
+- **Location**: `.dvc/cache_local`
+- **Default**: Yes
+
+### Adding Additional Remotes
+
+For production or team collaboration, you can add cloud storage remotes:
+
+#### AWS S3
+```bash
+poetry run dvc remote add -d s3remote s3://my-bucket/dvc-storage
+poetry run dvc remote modify s3remote region us-east-1
+```
+
+#### Google Cloud Storage
+```bash
+poetry run dvc remote add -d gcsremote gs://my-bucket/dvc-storage
+poetry run dvc remote modify gcsremote projectname my-project
+```
+
+#### SSH/SFTP
+```bash
+poetry run dvc remote add -d sshremote ssh://user@example.com/path/to/dvc-storage
+```
+
+### List Remotes
+```bash
+poetry run dvc remote list
+```
+
+## CI/CD Integration
+
+In CI pipelines, datasets can be pulled automatically:
+
+```yaml
+# Example GitHub Actions workflow
+steps:
+  - name: Setup DVC
+    run: poetry install --with dev,ml
+
+  - name: Pull datasets
+    run: poetry run dvc pull
+
+  - name: Run tests
+    run: poetry run pytest
+```
+
+## Best Practices
+
+1. **Never commit large files to Git** - Always use DVC for files >10MB
+2. **Commit .dvc files to Git** - These small metadata files belong in version control
+3. **Use meaningful dataset names** - Make it clear what each dataset contains
+4. **Document dataset changes** - Include details in commit messages when updating .dvc files
+5. **Regular cleanup** - Use `dvc gc` to remove unused data from cache
+
+## Troubleshooting
+
+### Dataset Not Found
+```bash
+# Pull from remote
+poetry run dvc pull data/training/iqa_phase2.dvc
+```
+
+### Cache Issues
+```bash
+# Verify cache
+poetry run dvc cache dir
+
+# Rebuild cache
+poetry run dvc cache rebuild
+```
+
+### Permission Errors
+```bash
+# Fix permissions on cache
+chmod -R u+w .dvc/cache
+```
+
+## Integration with Project Phases
+
+- **Phase 2 (Current)**: IQA training dataset tracked (`data/training/iqa_phase2`)
+- **Phase 3**: YOLOv8 layout detection datasets (to be added)
+- **Phase 4+**: Additional datasets as needed
+
+## References
+
+- [DVC Documentation](https://dvc.org/doc)
+- [DVC with Poetry](https://dvc.org/doc/install/poetry)
+- [DVC Remote Storage](https://dvc.org/doc/command-reference/remote)
+

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

**Ensure label tensor shapes match `MultiHeadIQALoss` expectations**

`collate_fn` currently builds per‑head labels as 1D tensors:

```python
batch_dict["labels"][head_name] = labels_batch[:, idx]
batch_dict["confidence"][head_name] = torch.ones_like(labels_batch[:, idx])
```

`ResNetTeacher` heads typically output `(batch, 1)` tensors, and the `MultiHeadIQALoss` implementation was written with `(batch, 1)` targets in mind. If the loss doesn’t internally reshape targets to match logits, you’ll get unintended broadcasting (`(B, 1)` vs `(B,)`) in BCE/MSE.

It would be safer to explicitly match shapes, e.g.:

```diff
-        for idx, head_name in enumerate(issue_types):
-            batch_dict["labels"][head_name] = labels_batch[:, idx]
-            # Use full confidence (1.0) for all labels
-            batch_dict["confidence"][head_name] = torch.ones_like(labels_batch[:, idx])
+        for idx, head_name in enumerate(issue_types):
+            per_head = labels_batch[:, idx].unsqueeze(1)  # (B, 1)
+            batch_dict["labels"][head_name] = per_head
+            # Use full confidence (1.0) for all labels
+            batch_dict["confidence"][head_name] = torch.ones_like(per_head)
```

Please double‑check the current `MultiHeadIQALoss` signature and adjust if it already normalizes shapes internally.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Fix exception handler using `epoch` before it’s guaranteed to exist**

The `try` block wraps the entire epoch loop, but the `except` handler logs:

```python
except Exception as e:
    print(f"\n❌ Training failed at epoch {epoch + 1}: {e}")
    raise
```

If an exception is raised before the first `for epoch in range(total_epochs)` iteration (e.g., in config lookup, device setup, or DataLoader construction), `epoch` will be undefined and you’ll mask the original error with an `UnboundLocalError`.

A more robust pattern:

```diff
-    try:
-        # Manual epoch loop for better progress visibility
-        for epoch in range(total_epochs):
+    current_epoch = 0
+    try:
+        # Manual epoch loop for better progress visibility
+        for epoch in range(total_epochs):
+            current_epoch = epoch + 1
             ...
-    except Exception as e:
-        print(f"\n❌ Training failed at epoch {epoch + 1}: {e}")
-        raise
+    except Exception as e:
+        print(f"\n❌ Training failed at epoch {current_epoch or 'N/A'}: {e}")
+        raise
```

This preserves meaningful context without risking a secondary exception.

references epoch which may not be defined if an error occurs before the loop;

log "epoch N/A" when epoch is None, then re-raise the original exception—this
avoids an UnboundLocalError while preserving the original error message.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🔴 Critical_

**Fix misuse of `shlex.quote` in `download_from_gcs` subprocess call**

`download_from_gcs` builds `gcs_path` and `nfs_path` using `shlex.quote` but then passes them as individual arguments in a list to `subprocess.run` with `shell=False`. This means the literal single quotes become part of the arguments, so `gsutil rsync` will see invalid URLs/paths and likely fail. Since you’re not invoking a shell, quoting here is unnecessary and harmful.  


A minimal fix:

```diff
-    # Sanitize paths to prevent command injection (defensive coding)
-    gcs_path = shlex.quote(config["gcs_path"])
-    nfs_path = shlex.quote(str(config["nfs_path"]) + "/")
-
-    cmd = [
-        "gsutil",
-        "-m",
-        "rsync",
-        "-r",
-        gcs_path,
-        nfs_path,
-    ]
+    # Paths are static definitions from this module; pass them directly
+    gcs_path = config["gcs_path"]
+    nfs_path = str(config["nfs_path"]) + "/"
+
+    cmd = [
+        "gsutil",
+        "-m",
+        "rsync",
+        "-r",
+        gcs_path,
+        nfs_path,
+    ]
```

Keeping `shell=False` with unquoted strings is both safe and functionally correct here since all inputs come from trusted constants.
